reason: Research this week found an AI and semiconductor selloff with Nvidia weakness, a software selloff on fears that AI agents will pressure subscription pricing, and a Fed that already hiked in September with a possible further hike being priced in after hotter October inflation. I could not confirm a same-day catalyst for the 11-20 close, and I did not find a clean reason to add risk or to rotate the core. The core SPY and VTV anchors and the JPM and KO defensives stay as they are, since replacing them now would cost churn on thin evidence. Two legs are worth noting. The SQQQ short is a mismatched hedge: shorting an inverse Nasdaq ETF is effectively a long Nasdaq bet, and it is down 42.8 percent, so this is a known drag of roughly 1.3 percent of NAV that I am choosing to carry rather than realise into a choppy tape. BTC spot at 4 percent is down about 22 percent year to date, and I am not adding to it. Stops on the core legs are absent by design. I will revisit if the Fed hike path firms or if the software and semiconductor selloff broadens further. Searches were limited to about five queries, and the sources were mixed in date quality, so this is a judgement on partial research.
